:::{figure} generated/validation/tier1.png
:label: fig-tier1
:class: col-page

tier1: one 4 m undulator segment of the Aramis line in steady state from a 5 kW seed, with no interlude, so the FEL core alone: the push, the deposition and the field solve. Genesis4 is the solid line and Lucifer the dashed line over it, and δ is Lucifer's value less Genesis4's. (a) The power on a linear and a log axis, and δP/P at each record. (b) The bunching, and its difference over the peak bunching. (c) The mean energy change from the first record, and its difference over the largest change. (d) The field amplitude along the row through the center of the exit plane at s = 4 m, and its difference over the peak amplitude. The largest differences are 8.3e-8 in power, 5.2e-7 in bunching, 3.0e-4 in energy and 4.6e-7 in the field row. The tier's level is 1.83e-6 against a tolerance of 1e-4, set by the complex field at the exit over the whole grid, 1.83e-6 of its peak. [Full size](generated/validation/tier1.png).
:::

:::{figure} generated/validation/tier1_unavg.png
:label: fig-tier1-unavg
:class: col-page

tier1_unavg: the same segment with the unaveraged dynamics, whose model differs from Genesis4's in its sin² end ramps, its lack of period averaging and its integrator, so the tier holds a model difference and shows a drift. (b) The bunching, and its difference over the peak bunching. (c) The mean energy change from the first record, and its difference over the largest change. (d) The field amplitude along the row through the center of the exit plane at s = 4 m, and its difference over the peak amplitude. The largest differences are 6.2e-3 in power, 7.3e-3 in bunching, 1.7e-2 in energy and 1.4e-2 in the field row. The tier's level is 6.98e-2 against a tolerance of 1e-1, set by the complex field at the exit over the whole grid, 6.98e-2 of its peak. [Full size](generated/validation/tier1_unavg.png).
:::

:::{figure} generated/validation/td1.png
:label: fig-td1
:class: col-page

td1: one segment time dependent, 32 slices of three wavelengths from a 5 kW seed: the FEL core with slippage. Genesis4 is the solid line and Lucifer the dashed line over it, and δ is Lucifer's value less Genesis4's. (a) The energy in the window on a linear and a log axis, and under it the power difference at each record over the reference's power, the one over the slices of largest magnitude. (b) The slice-mean bunching, and the largest slice difference over the peak bunching. (c) The slice-mean energy change from the first record, and the largest slice difference over the largest change. (d) The power across the window at the exit, s = 4 m, slice by slice, and its difference over the peak exit power. The largest differences are 8.4e-7 in power, 8.4e-8 in bunching, 8.5e-7 in energy and 8.3e-7 in the exit power. The tier's level is 8.36e-7 against a tolerance of 1e-4, set by the power. [Full size](generated/validation/td1.png).
:::

:::{figure} generated/validation/weight_split.png
:label: fig-weight-split
:class: col-page

weight_split: tier1 run again with the particles' weights split nonuniformly, drawn over tier1 itself, Lucifer over Lucifer. A collective observable is linear in the weights, so the two must agree to round-off, which Genesis4's dumps cannot test since they carry no weights. tier1 is the solid line and tier1, weights split the dashed line over it, and δ is tier1, weights split's value less tier1's. (a) The power on a linear and a log axis, and δP/P at each record. (b) The bunching, and its difference over the peak bunching. (c) The mean energy change from the first record, and its difference over the largest change. (d) The field amplitude along the row through the center of the exit plane at s = 4 m, and its difference over the peak amplitude. The largest differences are 8.1e-16 in power, 3.5e-13 in bunching, 0 in energy and 6.9e-15 in the field row. The tier's level is 3.54e-13 against a tolerance of 1e-10, set by the bunching. [Full size](generated/validation/weight_split.png).
:::
